body: If this is deemed harmless, I would probably just make `GodotSpace2D::body_add_to_state_query_list` check and silently not add an object that's already in the queue, like [this](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/compare/master...mgiuca:godot:body-state-query-list-error).

> If this is deemed harmless, I would probably just make `GodotSpace2D::body_add_to_state_query_list` check and silently not add an object that's already in the queue, like [this](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/compare/master...mgiuca:godot:body-state-query-list-error).

I personally don't feel this is harmless (running step twice without flush, without the developers knowledge). It breaks the cycle order and may cause issues for some games that might be hard to find. So I would want people to see an error if they do this.


> The problem is that "Condition "p_elem->_root" is true" happens whenever a SelfList is added to a list when it is already in a list, and since there are hundreds of uses of SelfList across the code base, the same error message pops up whenever it is misused. I would find it useful if this error message was augmented with the typeid of the element type, which would give individual bug reports a distinctive signature. (Eerily similar to a PR I put up recently, https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122156, to do the same thing in another part of the codebase.)

That sounds like a great PR! I have seen this uninformative error a number of times now.

## Main loop zone checking
I have seen enough of these "Don't call X() from _process or call_deferred" issues that I strongly believe we should do something about it. I think when we know X() should not be called from y() then we should have a way to enforce that and make it an error. How to do that exactly is a proposal in itself.

One quick guess would be that we declare an enum for the particular 'main loop zone' we are in within the code along with some macros that can warn or error specifically about zone compliance. So for any physics body access functions we could add `ASSERT_ZONE(ZONE_PROCESS_PHYSICS || ZONE_INTEGRATE_FORCES)` which will fail with an error or warning if the user calls them from _process(). The pause setter we might need something like 
```
if (pause == false && zone != pause_zone) {
    ERROR_PRINT("Unpausing in a different zone of the main loop could cause undefined behaviour")
}
```
Then we might need a way that you can call something regardless of what zone you are in (if people really need to be 'unsafe').

I think this problem of not knowing when it is safe to make a particular type of call in gdScript was one of the most flaky things about Godot when I first picked it up, and the only hope of understanding it was to dig into engine source. I don't think documentation can solve this, but zone checking could.

Static zone checking would be better, but it doesn't mean that we couldn't do dynamic zone checking for now, and just remove that code if we ended up with better static checks for zone compliance.
Forgot to add that I did test this MRP and can confirm the "Condition "p_elem->_root" is true" error print that you mentioned.
